name: Arcadia-Wound
geological_features: Broad temperate forest basins separated by low mountain ranges
River delta systems feeding nutrient-rich floodplains
Exposed clear-cut zones where topsoil erosion has carved deep gullies into former forestland
specific_features: Industrial logging scars visible from orbit as geometric brown patches amid green canopy
Silt plumes extending hundreds of kilometers into the coastal ocean from erosion runoff
The Mourning Stands, isolated pockets of old-growth forest surrounded by stripped land
resources: Hardwood timber species with exceptional structural properties
Medicinal compounds derived from old-growth canopy flora
Freshwater reserves in the mountain aquifer systems
description: Arcadia-Wound was once among the most beautiful terrestrial worlds in the catalogued systems, a planet of vast temperate forests whose canopy stretched unbroken across three continents and whose biodiversity rivaled any world yet surveyed. The forests remain, but they are diminished, carved into geometric sections by industrial logging operations that have stripped entire watersheds to bare soil. From orbit, the damage is stark: brown scars cut into green, erosion gullies running like open veins, and silt plumes clouding coastal waters that were once crystalline.

The atmosphere remains clean in the intact forest zones, carrying the scent of resin and wet earth and alive with the calls of canopy fauna. But on the edges of the logging zones, the air tastes of dust and exposed mineral soil, and the silence is conspicuous. The Mourning Stands, those isolated pockets of old-growth forest that survived by accident of terrain or bureaucratic oversight, have become refugia for species whose habitat has been reduced by ninety percent in three decades. Their canopy trees are centuries old, towering and cathedral-dark, surrounded on all sides by stumps and mud.

The exploitation of Arcadia-Wound was driven by the exceptional structural properties of its native hardwoods, which resist fatigue and radiation degradation in ways that synthetic materials cannot match. A colonial charter granted exclusive harvesting rights to a timber consortium that operated with minimal environmental oversight for decades. By the time independent surveys documented the scale of ecological collapse, the consortium had extracted sufficient profit to afford the legal battles that followed, tying conservation orders up in jurisdictional disputes.

The planet's fauna includes several species found nowhere else, three of which are now critically endangered as their forest habitat fragments into ever-smaller islands. Conservation groups maintain a small orbital presence and conduct guerrilla reforestation drops, but the legal status of the planet remains contested. Arcadia-Wound has become a symbol in broader political debates about resource extraction and ecological responsibility, its scarred surface a visible argument that can be seen from space.
